command: claude --permission-mode manual (interactive TUI, driven under a pty), with a project-local .claude/settings.json registering PermissionRequest
note: The gate is `PermissionRequest`, NOT `Notification`: the only Notification this run fired was the idle `Claude is waiting for your input`. The composed fixture's belief that a permission arrives as Notification is what let install/claude.rs ship without registering PermissionRequest at all — the decoder has always handled it, the bytes just never arrived. Home path redacted to /Users/dev. Redacted: the recorder's own MCP server / skill inventory (tool NAMES only, no credentials) to generic placeholders — a public repo and an immutable crates.io tarball are the wrong home for one machine's tooling roster, and no decoder reads those fields. Redacted: the recorder's installed plugin roster — skill and agent names, their descriptions, and the install paths that give the names back — to `example-skill-N` / `example-plugin-N:example-agent` placeholders, collapsed to three entries because the COUNT is this machine's inventory size too. Each CLI's own bundled set is kept, told apart mechanically rather than by a name list: a `:` in a claude-code agent type means plugin-provided, copilot tags `<location>builtin</location>`, codex roots its own at `r2/` or `.codex/skills/.system/`. No decoder reads any of these fields and every conformance golden is byte-identical.
